correctness.rationale: The likelihood-ratio representations are \(W_i=e^{-\delta_n^2/2+\delta_nZ_i}\) and \(W_*=e^{\delta_n^2/2+\delta_nZ_*}\). Below \(\beta=2\), the Gaussian maximum gives a source-weight exponent exceeding the target exponent. Above it, the stated fractional-moment/Markov choice gives a strictly negative exponent and forces \(S_n/W_*\to0\). At criticality, truncating calibration weights at \(n\) gives exactly \(E A_i=1/2\), \(E A_i^2=n^2\bar\Phi(\sqrt{2\log n})\), whence \(S_n/n\to1/2\), while \(W_*/n=e^{\sqrt{2\log n}Z_*}\) tends to zero or infinity by the sign of \(Z_*\). The weighted-quantile infinity event is therefore exactly controlled by this atom.

value.rationale: The result turns a practical failure mode of weighted conformal prediction—an infinite quantile/all-real prediction set—into a sharp overlap phase transition and identifies a nondegenerate critical law. This materially refines the generic KL heuristic on a canonical model.

final_claim: For Gaussian covariate shift \(P=N(0,1)\), \(Q_n=N(\delta_n,1)\), the weighted-conformal test-point mass at \(+\infty\) tends to \(0\) when \(\delta_n^2/\log n\to\beta<2\), to \(1\) when \(\beta>2\), and at \(\delta_n=\sqrt{2\log n}\) converges to \(\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2)\); equivalently the infinite-quantile transition occurs at \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q_n\|P)=\log n\).
limitations: The exact critical law is proved only at the exact scaling \(\delta_n=\sqrt{2\log n}\), not a second-order critical window.
One-dimensional equal-variance Gaussian shift and exact likelihood ratios only.
The theorem characterizes the infinite-quantile event, not finite interval widths below threshold.
